guard: The shipped conformance corpus is a real artifact: the accessor serves exactly what is on disk, and every recorded verdict is one the validator still gives. (FAIL-FAST suite: markers are upstream of the cells they guard.)

mutations.name: the accessor drops a case and still reports the corpus
mutations.find: const cases = list.map((c, i) => checkCase(c, i + 1));
mutations.replace: const cases = list.slice(1).map((c, i) => checkCase(c, i + 1));
mutations.expectRed: the accessor serves the artifact as it is on disk
mutations.completionMarker: the shipped artifact parses to a cases array
mutations.cell: the accessor serves the artifact as it is on disk
mutations.note: A reader that silently drops or reshapes cases would ship a corpus that is not the artifact; the disk-agreement cell is what refuses that.

mutations.name: a verdict in the artifact drifts from what the validator answers
mutations.expectRed: every recorded verdict holds against the validator today
mutations.completionMarker: the corpus carries at least seven cases, acceptance and refusal both
mutations.cell: every recorded verdict holds against the validator today
mutations.note: L1030 is a real catalog code the class block cannot produce, so the accessor still serves the mutated artifact and the verdict re-check is the cell that has to notice.
